results.claim: Same-game correlation: home ATS cover x over
results.formula: read from the committed corr_same_game.csv; R12 re-derives the same quantity from the underlying per-game indicator columns

results.claim: Same-game correlation re-derived independently from model_dataset.csv
results.formula: Pearson phi of the dataset's own home_cover and over indicator columns (non-push rows only, n = 6784)
results.note: An earlier draft of this check rebuilt the indicators as (margin + spread_line > 0) and ignored the dataset's push convention, which gave -0.0072 and looked like a disagreement. Using the dataset's own columns reproduces the published 0.0086 exactly. The draft error is recorded here on purpose: an independent check that cannot report its own mistakes is not a check.

results.claim: Break-even correlation a 2-leg parlay needs at -110 per leg (each leg a true coin flip)
results.formula: P(both) = p^2 + phi*sqrt(p(1-p)p(1-p)); break-even needs P(both) = 1/decimal; p = 0.5, decimal = (1+100/110)^2 = 4.41
results.note: The repository's formula and this independent one agree to six decimal places at p = 0.5, where sqrt(p(1-p)p(1-p)) and p(1-p) are both 0.25. An earlier draft of this check divided by the wrong quantity and wrongly reported a defect; that error is recorded, not deleted.

results.claim: Break-even correlation for a 3-leg parlay at -110 (as published)
results.note: The published 0.0749 is correct and this independent recomputation agrees. Recorded here because this session's own draft check went through THREE wrong versions: it first divided by 2.1^3 instead of (1+100/110)^3 = 1.909^3, then reported the wrong sign, then wrongly called the committed JSON stale. Each was caught by recomputing before publication and none was published as a repo defect. Retained verbatim because a verification log that hides its own retractions is worth less than one that shows them.
